_comment: Players who join the WNBA pool REGARDLESS of the MPG>=16 / G>=20 rule. This file COMPOSES with that rule rather than replacing it: scripts/cardgen/wnba/generateWnbaCards.js keeps everyone the rule already admits and adds everyone named here, so an entry can only ever ADD a player. Keyed by the player name exactly as Basketball-Reference's WNBA per-game table spells it; a name matching no row is reported and the run exits non-zero rather than leaving the pool quietly one player short. WHY THESE SEVEN: every one of them clears the MPG half of the rule and is dropped by the G>=20 half alone — the half that cannot tell a bad player from a short season. Six are injury exceptions, and were chosen against the standard the NBA pool's were: a 25+ MPG player when healthy. THE SEVENTH, DiJonai Carrington, IS A DIRECT USER PICK and is NOT that player — 16.2 MPG off the Chicago bench in 2026, 21.9 across Dallas and Minnesota in 2025 — so she is recorded here as what she is rather than dressed up as an injury case. What makes her cardable on the same terms is the blend below: 11 games is too thin, 42 is not. Deliberately still NOT included: Rickea Jackson (4 G) and Kara Dunn (1 G), whose samples are too thin to card on EVEN WITH a blend. THEIR NUMBERS ARE BLENDED, unlike the NBA's: each of these seven is carded on 2025 AND 2026 pooled by volume, per stat, against the denominator each stat is a rate over (possessions for per-100 and rate percentages, the relevant attempts for each shooting percentage, minutes for per-four-minute production, sums for season totals). That blend is possible here and blocked on the NBA side for one reason only — Basketball-Reference publishes WNBA 2025 in full and for free, where dunksandthrees paywalls prior NBA seasons. See scripts/cardgen/wnba/pool.js.
DiJonai Carrington: user pick, not an injury case: 11 G at 16.2 MPG in 2026, blended with 31 G at 21.9 in 2025
